approach: Adopt a pinned prebuilt cargo-nextest behind ONE check named `test`, whose command is the xtask wrapper `cargo run --locked -q -p xtask -- test`. The wrapper runs the pinned nextest binary by absolute path (`cargo-nextest nextest run --locked`), then `cargo test --doc --locked`. It runs both halves and exits nonzero if either fails. If the pinned binary is not installed (a machine not yet re-setup), it prints a clear warning and falls back to `cargo test --locked`, so no check breaks at rollout and every test still runs. Athena's test counter and failing-test reader learn nextest's output. Producers, verifiers and demonstrations use the wrapper, which `cargo run` already permits. The pin values are not knowable inside this job (no network), so the plan marks them unverified until someone with network access supplies them; CI on the pull request is the first real check.

decisions.choice: One `test` check backed by an xtask `test` wrapper (nextest, then doctests); no separate doctest check.
decisions.reason: CI STEPS is fmt/clippy/test and routing reuses CI results by check name, so one check leaves them unchanged. A nonzero exit from either half fails the wrapper and so the check.

rejected.why: Needs STEPS, xtask ci, routing and ci_result changes; wider scope.
Check commands are argv lists; exit handling would be hidden.

decisions.choice: Rollout by graceful fallback: if tools/nextest/<ver>/cargo-nextest is absent, the wrapper warns on stderr and runs `cargo test --locked` instead. The CHANGELOG and decision also tell the user to run ./setup.sh after landing to get the speedup. A unit test covers the missing-binary branch and the present-binary path resolution.
decisions.reason: Checks run from the base commit's athena.toml and setup refuses to run inside a job (ATHENA_NESTED), so a check cannot install the tool. Failing every later job until setup is run is worse than a slow-but-correct run. Nothing is filtered: the fallback runs the whole suite.

rejected.option: Fail loudly when the binary is missing
rejected.why: Every later job's test check would fail until a manual setup; no way to self-heal.

rejected.option: Put the pinned binary on agents' PATH
rejected.why: Changes env passing for governance-sensitive sandboxes; wrapper by absolute path needs none.

decisions.choice: Producers, verifiers and demonstrations run `cargo run --locked -q -p xtask -- test` (already allowed). Do NOT add `nextest` to the cargo allow-lists.
decisions.reason: `cargo nextest` needs cargo-nextest on PATH, which the tools directory is not; an allow-list entry would permit a command that fails with 'no such command'.

rejected.option: Add `nextest` to producer and verifier cargo subcommands
rejected.why: The command would not resolve on PATH.

decisions.choice: Producer guidance: add one sentence to the producer brief guidance in crates/athena-core/src/run.rs (or the briefs source if the guidance text lives in athena-context; locate by grep for `cargo test` first): 'run the full suite with `cargo run --locked -q -p xtask -- test`; for one test use `cargo test -p <crate> <name>`'. The sentence is short and system_facts budgets are recomputed and the budget lines updated if the test system_facts_budgets_match_computed reports a difference.
decisions.reason: The request names producer time as a cost, and a producer must learn the faster loop. This is unconditional, not 'if grep finds'.

rejected.why: Producers would never use the faster loop.

decisions.choice: Cut run time (673 s) not compile time (67 s) with cargo-nextest; nextest skips doctests so `cargo test --doc` runs them and every test still runs.
decisions.reason: Measured by the brain on 4 cores: compile 67 s via cargo test --no-run, run 673 s warm.

rejected.option: sccache per D79 for checks, producers and CI
rejected.why: Cuts only the 67 s compile side; out of scope.

rejected.option: Shared target directory for Athena's checks
rejected.why: Compile side only; weakens per-job isolation (D46); out of scope.

rejected.option: Splitting the slowest integration test binaries
rejected.why: Restructures tests (out of scope); fallback only if nextest cannot be installed.

decisions.choice: Pin via a new optional `nextest: Option<ToolPin>` in Tools (crates/athena-data/src/config.rs), version and sha256 per platform key, with a nextest-specific URL builder in xtask (linux gnu tar.gz; darwin universal tar.gz, same checksum for both darwin keys). The values are written by someone with network access from the release's published checksums; if unavailable, the producer records the pin as UNVERIFIED in the decision and CHANGELOG, and the PR's CI setup (which refuses a mismatch) is the first check. No value is guessed silently.
decisions.reason: deny_unknown_fields on Tools rejects an unknown [tools.nextest], so config.rs must change. checks.rs, gh.rs and config.rs are outside the brief's list but required: Tools has deny_unknown_fields (config.rs ~266-273); count_tests counts only libtest `test result:` lines and a Test-kind check with zero tests fails (checks.rs ~29-41, ~209-211). The decision entry states this justification so the verifier sees it.

rejected.why: No checksum and minutes of compile.
Breaks the pinned-tool pattern and the policy test over [tools].

decisions.choice: Keep the substring `cargo fmt --check` and `id: checks` in the ci.yml checks step; change only comments and add the nextest install via setup. Update policy tests only if they must change.
decisions.reason: xtask/tests/policy.rs ~537, 571, 575 find that step by name and id.

decisions.choice: Extend count_tests to read nextest `Summary [..] N tests run: N passed` and sum with libtest doctest lines; failing_test_name reads nextest `FAIL [..] name`. Unit tests use sample output supplied with the pin by someone with network access; if none is supplied, they use the format documented by nextest and the decision says the format is unverified against a real run.
decisions.reason: Without it every nextest check counts zero tests and fails (M12); keeping the zero guard preserves detection of an empty run.
